claim: For every integer \(r\ge 2\), let \(X=\mathbb P(1^r,a,b)\) with \(1\le a\le b\), and suppose \(X\) is canonical but not terminal. A general anticanonical hypersurface of degree \(D=r+a+b\) is quasismooth if and only if \((a,b)=(c,c+r)\) for a positive divisor \(c\) of \(2r\) or \(2r-1\), or \((a,b)=(r,r)\), or \((a,b)=(2r-1,3r-2)\). Consequently exactly \(\tau(2r)+\tau(2r-1)+1\) of the \(3r\) canonical non-terminal boundary spaces admit a quasismooth anticanonical hypersurface, where \(\tau(n)\) is the number of positive divisors of \(n\).
integrity: The all-dimensional classification is proved symbolically from the coordinate-stratum monomial criterion and the canonical/terminal boundary inequalities. Exact enumeration through \(r=150\) is a regression check only.
scientific_limitations: Restricted to complete anticanonical hypersurfaces on ordinary weighted projective spaces of the form \(\mathbb P(1^r,a,b)\) lying on the canonical non-terminal boundary; no statement is made for higher codimension, fake weighted projective spaces, or off-boundary weights.
title: Quasismooth anticanonical sections on the canonical non-terminal two-heavy boundary
